title: Turn on Peer AI's security pipeline, so dependencies are actually watched
goal: DEL-03 has failed on two items: nothing checks dependencies for vulnerabilities on change or on a schedule, and npm audit reports 19 advisories with 5 critical. Peer AI already ships the answer in its github-actions stack profile, which this project does not list: osv-scanner for dependencies, gitleaks pinned by checksum, zizmor for the workflows, Semgrep for the code, on every pull request and daily. Adopt it in reporting mode first, as the lint rules were adopted.
acceptance: Given the github-actions profile is added and render runs, when the workflow is written, then every job it contains is read and named before it is committed, and anything inapplicable — a TLS or running-app scan for a product with no deployed environment — is absent rather than disabled

Given the pipeline runs on this pull request, when it reports, then the dependency job's findings are recorded with their severities, so the 19 advisories are a list in the repository rather than a number in a conversation
Given the pipeline is adopted in reporting mode, when a job finds something, then it warns and stays green, and what it would take to make each job block is written down

Given gitleaks is now pinned by checksum in the new workflow, when the old gitleaks-action@v2 step in pr-checks.yml is considered, then the duplication is resolved one way or the other rather than left running twice
Given DEL-03's open finding on ITEM-9 and ITEM-10, when this lands, then the finding is closed with the evidence that a scheduled and per-change scan now exists

reviews.summary: Pass, light depth as the required review asked. One hunk, eleven comment lines and a rule-specific suppression above an unchanged statement, so no behaviour could change. The claim the comment makes was measured at five input sizes up to 100,001 characters rather than asserted, and the suppression names one rule id rather than silencing the tool.

Pass, light depth. The change strengthens security rather than touching an attack surface: four unpinned actions pinned to commits, two persisted job credentials dropped, a mutable gitleaks action replaced by a checksum-verified binary, and dependency scanning introduced where there was none. The one code hunk is a comment and a rule-specific suppression, with the claim behind it measured.

Pass. The change adds four CI checks and tightens the two that existed: permissions: {} at the top of the new workflow with contents: read per job, every tool pinned by checksum, digest or commit, four unpinned actions pinned, and the job credential no longer persisted in two checkouts. Seven of thirteen rules do not apply because there is no server, no second environment and nothing deployed.

Pass, all five criteria on observed evidence. Every job was seen failing before it was trusted: the first run failed three of three, the second still failed zizmor on two medium findings, and only the third passed. The 19 advisories are now a named list in the config and in ITEM-12 rather than a number, the gitleaks duplication is resolved by one checksum-verified tool, and only the dependencies job reports.
